Header:
Date: 2026-07-21
Start: 09:23 PDT
Duration: 1:15:00
Attendees: Maya (PM), Ravi (Eng Mgr), Olivia (SRE), Ethan (Tech PM), Diego (Lead SWE)
Links shared: Q3-launch-checklist (internal doc), perf-bench-results (sheet, provisional), runbooks/runbook-kv-warmup.md

Summary:
Quick sync to validate Q3 launch readiness: review outstanding engineering tasks, incident follow-up from the Q2 perf regression, finalize canary metrics and dashboards, confirm who owns what for the go/no-go on Aug 3. Several references to the Redwood dedicted (sic) pool and the KV cash (typo: KV cache) warmup script.

Transcript:
[09:23] Maya (PM): okay everyone's here? cool, um let me kick off, this is our Q3 launch readiness sync so the goal is to close blockers and make sure we all agree on go/no-go gating, right?
[09:24] Ravi (Eng): yep, that and to validate the perf regression follow-up, we had that p95 blip last month, still seeing some tail lat concerns under certain seq-len distributions
[09:25] Olivia (SRE): right, during the spike on june 14 we saw a KV cache thrash when some prefixes were cold; our autoscaler also didn't kick fast enough, so we had elevated queueing for about 6 minutes
[09:26] Maya: quick context — this launch targets two new enterprise customers and we need dedicated pools available plus VPC onboarding docs, so we need the dedicated capacity aka Redwood Dedicated to be predictable, devs to have the warmup tooling, and SRE to own the runbook
[09:27] Ethan (Tech PM): i'll share the consolidated checklist after this call; includes security signoffs, KMS config, SOC2 docs reference, and acceptance criteria for perf and error rates
[09:28] Diego: on the KV cache side, i've got a warmup script that does prefix prefetch plus a small synthetic traffic pattern, we need to test it against the dedicated pool and the quantized model variant — the performance changes a little with quantization but should be fine
[09:30] Speaker 1 (might be Ravi): can we re-confirm the exact gating numbers? like p95 under 300ms for the 512 token median, and p99 under 900ms? those are the thresholds we discussed in the pre-meeting notes
[09:31] Maya: yes, p95 < 300ms, p99 < 900ms for normal load; for burst scenarios we allow p99 up to 1.2s but we prefer to keep it below 1s. Also error rate target < 0.5% and no more than 2 sustained minutes > error budget in any 1h window
[09:32] Olivia: got it, i'll put those on the new grafana panels; i'll also add an alert if the error budget burn rate exceeds x10 in 5 mins
[09:34] Ravi: for the perf regression — quick recap: in Q2 we rolled a runtime kernel switch that reduced median latency overall but in some cases the KV cache eviction pattern changed and caused cache misses; that manifested as p95 spikes when sequence lengths were higher than our training dist. we reverted the kernel for the last week while we instrumented more traces
[09:35] Diego: we also noticed the sequence length distribution we used in CI didn't match production; we were using 256 median but prod med is like 420-500 for these customers, so the cache behavior is different
[09:36] Maya: action: Diego, update CI dist to include 400+ seq lengths and run perf matrix; Ravi run the bench on dedicated dev pool too
[09:37] Diego: yeah, i can run that. estimating 24-36h for the matrix given current queue, unless we bump priority. also the warmup script needs to be integrated into the deploy pipeline so the pool warms on scale-up
[09:38] Ethan: regarding rollout strategy — we recommended canary with traffic ramp for 48h at 5% then 25% then full; we should monitor p95/p99, error rate, and user-facing correctness metrics. if any of the following hit — p99 > 1s or error rate > 1% for 10m — we rollback automatically
[09:40] Olivia: please note our canary automation hooks into the console, but we need the new panels and the error budget alerts to be live before we do the canary. i'll need about 3 days to get the dashboards solid and run the alert tests
[09:41] Ravi: on the dedicated capacity config — one question: do we allow burst to shared capacity during outages? Product asked for cross-fallback but security wanted isolation for the enterprise customers
[09:42] Maya: enterprise customers want strict isolation, so default is no fallback to shared for those tenants; but for non-production we can allow fallback to reduce cost. For the initial launch we should enforce isolation and maybe offer a limited spare capacity pool for emergencies
[09:43] Diego: that means we need predictable autoscaling and a margin on the dedicated pool; i'll propose a 20% buffer for the SLA day-0 config
[09:44] Ethan: that ties into cost modelling; if we reserve 20% buffer we need to show the finance impact to pricing — i'll add that to the checklist to share with GTM
[09:46] Maya: security and compliance check — SOC2 docs are ready but we still need SSO/SAML testing and KMS key rotation docs. Olivia, are we ok for SSO tests?
[09:47] Olivia: SSO tests in staging are passing, but I haven't executed a full purple team test with customer simulated traffic. i'll schedule one next week and include KMS rotation validation in it
[09:48] Ravi: another technical deep-dive note — our runtime kernel selector sometimes chooses a quantized path that is faster but the output token probability distribution shifts subtly for some prompts, that flagged in the eval harness. we need the eval team to confirm no quality regressions. not a blocker necessarily but a risk to surface to customers
[09:49] Diego: right, we should tie the eval regression checks to the rollout gate: if eval metric delta > threshold we block rollout and trigger manual review
[09:50] Maya: add that to the checklist: eval delta threshold, and which prompts we use for regression detection — Ethan can attach the prompt set link
[09:51] Ethan: i'll attach it and the eval scoring spreadsheet after the call; also adding the security packet link and the pricing impact worksheet
[09:52] Speaker 2 (Ethan): small ops ask — we should prepare runbooks for customer on-boarding: VPC setup, firewall rules, KMS steps, RBAC roles. i'll draft and we can iterate
[09:54] Olivia: incident review quick bit — the june 14 incident root cause was a combination of cache warmup + autoscaler thresholding; postmortem suggests two mitigations: 1) warmup script for prefixes and 2) lower autoscaler threshold under coldstart scenarios
[09:55] Ravi: we'll implement both; Diego will make warmup script, and SRE will tune the autoscaler policy; will also add a test harness to exercise cold-start scenario in CI
[09:56] Diego: note: warmup adds some cost because it generates synthetic tokens; we can control it by sampling prefixes from recent traffic and limiting to top-100 prefixes per tenant
[09:58] Maya: good tradeoff. for the go/no-go on Aug 3 we need: perf bench pass on dedicated pool, warmup integrated, SRE dashboards & alerts, SOC2 + SSO test signoff, and runbook + onboarding doc. If any major item is missing we push launch
[09:59] Ethan: timeline check — bench & warmup results by 7/25, dashboards by 7/28, security signoff by 7/30; that gives us a few days buffer before 8/3
[10:00] Olivia: agreed. i'll post the dashboard links in the checklist thread and tag owners
[10:02] Ravi: i want to flag a performance unknown with quantized model at high concurrencies — Diego can run concurrency sweeps but we should also plan a small customer-facing benchmark to validate expected tail behavior
[10:03] Diego: i'll do the concurrency sweeps on the dev dedicated pool, and if results look good we can run a short customer sim at 5% canary during the rollout
[10:04] Maya: any blockers from legal or procurement? we need to ensure contracts for dedicated capacity are queued
[10:05] Ethan: procurement says pricing template is ready, legal needs the final SOC2 artifacts; i'm coordinating with them and will escalate if missing
[10:06] Speaker 1 (Ravi): small question — do we want to include automatic fallback to CPU-based encode path to reduce GPU pressure during flakiness? might be a safety net but may affect latency
[10:07] Olivia: fallback to CPU is okay as last resort but we'd prefer to degrade gracefully at the model layer rather than shift hardware; let's keep that as contingency and document behaviors in the runbook
[10:08] Maya: wrapping up — recap of who does what, and timeline. Ethan will share consolidated checklist by Friday 7/23; Ravi and Diego will run perf and warmup tests and post by 7/25; Olivia will have dashboards and alerting by 7/28; Maya will schedule the go/no-go 8/3 and coordinate Exec invites.
[10:09] Diego: noted; also i'll PR the warmup script and link it in checklist
[10:11] Maya: thanks everyone. quick note: docs link and perf sheets will be posted in the #launch-readiness channel. meeting adjourned.

End of transcript.

Notes about transcript quality: auto-transcription had a few misrecognized terms (Redwood Dedicated spelled as dedicted, KV cache flagged as KV cash in some spots).
